meta.title: Beautiful Idiot
meta.sub: in which an idiot is best man, and a bride says no
meta.logline: Ryuji asks Haru to be his best man. At the altar, Nana finally says no. Ryuji lets her go, Aya points the way, and on a ferry to a lighthouse, at sunset, Haru faints and Nana catches him.

shots.text: The dress fits. The press release is ready. The board is delighted. Hotel Kurosaki and Gozen Capital. A very beautiful merger.
You keep saying merger, Mister Togashi. The word is wedding.
In our family, my dear, those words have always meant the same thing.
Let me think about it. And then say yes. That's what we do.
Brother. I brought rice balls. Tuna mayonnaise. You said, come to your room and talk.
I did say that. Come in. Lev, this is Ryuji. Ryuji, this is Lev.
Your cactus is judging me.
He judges everyone. It's not personal.
I want you to be my best man. On Saturday. Stand next to me at the altar.
Me? Why me?
Because you're the only person who'll tell me the truth. If she looks at you during the vows, I'll know. I want to know.
And if she does look at me?
Then I've been counting the wrong window for twenty years.
I'll be there. I'll wear the duck tie.
God help us all.
The wedding jacket again. Second wedding this jacket has been to. The first one went very well, for thirty-one years.
Was Mrs. Kobayashi happy?
She said I talked too much and listened too little. Then she married me anyway. That's love, Mister Mishima. Somebody knows your worst thing and stays.
Free information. Last time ever. The bride has not slept in three days. My cousin does the hotel laundry. She's been sleeping with a book of sunsets.
Kenta, that's not information. That's a secret.
Same thing, if you're eleven.
Whatever happens at that wedding, you come home after. The rent can wait.
The rent can wait? Mister Kobayashi, are you all right?
Don't tell anyone. I'm writing it down so I remember I said it.
We're closed. For you, especially.
I brought you a book. Every story in it ends well. I checked. It took me all night.
You read a whole book of happy endings to apologise to me?
Grandma said, find her a book with a good ending. I couldn't find one, so I found twelve.
You're impossible.
Do you want to know what I wished for, at Tanabata? I wished that you'd be happy. It's a stupid wish. It's working against me.
I'm sorry, Aya.
Don't be. Somebody should get what they wish for. Now go away. I have twelve happy endings to read.
Aya. Will you come to the island one day? Grandma has three thousand books. Most of them have terrible endings. You'd love them.
Maybe. If the goat behaves.
The goat never behaves. That's his best quality.
Beauty will save the world. Idiot. It might, at that.
The chapel had four thousand roses, a string quartet, two hundred guests, eleven cameras, and one best man in a borrowed jacket and a tie with ducks on it.
Okay. Last bet. Ten thousand yen says she bolts.
I'm not betting. I'm just hoping.
I wrote a song for the getaway. Just in case. It's fast.
Look at the best man. He's smiling. Why is he smiling? His girlfriend is marrying someone else!
Because he isn't thinking about himself. He never is. That's what makes him dangerous.
Ryuji Gozen. Do you take Nana Kurosaki, and the associated assets, as your lawful wife?
I do.
She looked at the best man.
Nana Kurosaki. Do you take Ryuji Gozen?
Let me think about it.
Practise with me. Say no to something.
I beg your pardon?
No! No to the merger! No to the board! No to the dress, it itches! No, no, no!
Oh my god. I said it. I said no. In a church!
That's my cue! Hit it!
Pay up, everybody! Ten thousand yen! I told you she'd bolt!
Security! Bring her back! There are contracts!
Let her go, Togashi.
Mister Gozen, the merger...
I wanted someone to stay. I thought if I paid enough, she'd stay. That's not the same as love. Brother here taught me that over rice balls.
Go on, Haru. Go and find her. Before I change my mind.
Are you sure?
No. Go.
Thank you, brother. Keep the lighthouse. I'll keep the gold. It's heavy, but I'm getting used to it.

Hello. Yes, it's Togashi. Your daughter said no. To everything. In a church. ...No, sir. I'm not calling to complain. I'm calling because I think, for the first time, she's going to be fine. Perhaps you'd like to call her. On her birthday. Next year. It's in March.
Nana! Nana! Has anyone seen a bride? She's probably angry and very fast.
She ran past my shop ten minutes ago. In a wedding dress. Holding her shoes. She went to the ferry terminal.
Aya! Why are you helping me?
Because I read twelve happy endings last night, and I'd like to see one in real life. Go. Make it a good one.
Thank you, Aya! You're the kindest person who pretends not to be!
Idiot.
Haru? How did you... you ran? In that jacket?
Aya told me. Ryuji let me go. Kenta probably knows already. Mister Kobayashi will read about it by accident.
I said no, Haru. To everything. I don't have a hotel or a board or a plan. Where am I even going?
Where would you like to go?
Somewhere nobody can buy me.
I know a lighthouse. The rent is free, the goat is handsome, and my grandmother makes terrible tea.
...That sounds like the best place in the world.
You know I set fire to a hundred million yen and ran out of my own wedding. In one month.
You also pressed a bus bell, ate tuna mayonnaise, bought a secret chair and said no in a church. It's been a very full month.
When you say it like that, I sound wonderful.
I always say it like that. It's the same month either way. I just tell it from the good end.
Haru. Why did you never try to buy me? Not even with a book.
Because you're not a thing, Nana. You're a person who's tired. You don't buy tired people. You sit next to them until they can sleep.
Then sit next to me. It's a long ferry.
Welcome home, Haru. And who is this? She's wearing a wedding dress and no shoes.
Nana Kurosaki. I'm... his former employer. I fired myself.
Then you'll need a job. Do you know how to feed a goat?
I've never fed anything. I had staff for that.
You hold out your hand and you stand very still and you let it come to you. It's the same with most things.
He's coming. He's coming! He's eating my veil. Is that allowed?
He's very handsome. He's allowed almost anything.
Haru, your goat is eating my wedding dress and I've never been happier.
That's the law of goats.
Haru. I don't know how to be happy. I never learned. Everyone always bought it for me.
Neither did I, at first. You practise. Like saying no. Then one day you notice you're doing it without trying.
Will you practise with me?
Every day. At three in the morning, if you like. I'll be awake.
Oh no. The sunset. And you. Both at once. That's too much beautiful.
Got you. I've got you, idiot.
Nana. Is it Tuesday?
You fainted, idiot. In front of a sunset and a goat and your grandmother.
It was worth it. Did I miss anything?
Only me, saying something I've never said to anyone.
Oh no. Say it again. I wasn't conscious.
Later. At three in the morning. If you're awake.
It's whatever day you want.
Taku released the slow song with the rain in it. Nobody skipped the ending.
Sora won ten thousand yen, and spent it on a ferry ticket to visit a lighthouse.
Mister Togashi took his first holiday in thirty years. He did not enjoy it, but he tried.
Mika deleted forty thousand bots and lost forty thousand followers, and slept better.
Mister Kobayashi's tomatoes won second prize, and he wrote everything down.
Kenta started charging two rice balls for information. Inflation.
Aya Ishida put a new sign in her window: happy endings, half price.
Ryuji Gozen bought a cactus. He named it Brother.
And on a small island with one lighthouse, a very handsome goat, and three thousand and one books, lived a very happy woman.
And a very happy idiot.
Thank you for watching Beautiful Idiot. Grandma says hello. Professor says nothing, he's eating a doormat. And Lev says... Lev is a cactus. But he looks happy. Is it Tuesday? Good night!
